content:
I have a way of gleaning certain text near the cursor position in Lean4/vscode editor. I'm sending data from a definition to an external C++/Qt widgets app. It's for (currently displaying, but eventually interactive proofs involving) commutative diagrams such as:

/-! # Example 1: Commutative Triangle
Place your cursor on `sorry` below — the InfoView should render
a triangle diagram with vertices A, B, C and arrows f, g, h.
-/
example {C : Type*} [Category C] {A B D : C}
    (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ D) (h : A ⟶ D)
    (w : f ≫ g = h) : f ≫ g = h := by
  -- Look at the InfoView: you should see a commutative triangle!
  exact w

Problem is example is unnamed, so I wanted to refer to it in my external app, not by line number (which can shift around), but by the name "Example 1: Commutative Triangle" for example in the comment that will always be found right above it.

The name of the tool is Totopos, and it will be open source. So, what would be the standard "markup" for a formatted comment that gets parsed by an external, third-party tool? Something like:

/-! # [Totopos] Diagram Name
Diagram description
-/

Should I just make something up, and change it later when the users have a preference?

Here's a screenshot of what we've got so far:

Googling "markdown how to set tag of a section" reveals that there are no standard ways to do that, one way is to use certain markdown extension (not supported in doc-gen yet) and use syntax like ## My Section Name {#custom-tag-id}
@Jz Pan why can't I just do it ad-hoc?

Daniel Donnelly said:

why can't I just do it ad-hoc?

That's fine but I mean there are already some markdown dialects supporting this.
So if later we want to support this then you can migrate seamlessly.

Daniel Donnelly said:

Problem is example is unnamed, so I wanted to refer to it in my external app, not by line number (which can shift around), but by the name "Example 1: Commutative Triangle" for example in the comment that will always be found right above it.

In this case, currently, doc-gen will automatically assign the tag #Example-1-Commutative-Triangle to it, but it cannot be guaranteed if the section title contains non-alphanumeric characters.
